question: What causal characteristics describe the genuine emergence from destructive market episodes, and which are common versus regime-specific?
purpose: Descriptor discovery only. Characterize each true recovery independently before attempting generalization or fitting a reentry rule.
descriptor_families: price recovery: return from reference low, distance from trailing lows, 5/10/20-session returns
pullback structure: rolling adverse excursion, higher-low behavior, failure to revisit prior low
breadth: fraction positive 20-day trend, fraction above 200-day trend, breadth change and persistence
return structure: positive-day fraction, negative-day fraction, extreme-negative-day clustering
rebound quality: successful 5-day rebounds and persistence
trend geometry: EMA 20/50/100/160/200 gaps, slopes, bullish ordering/reclaims
volatility: realized volatility, VIX, VVIX and normalization
external stress: OFR Funding/Credit/Volatility levels and lagged changes
methodology: The reference trough is used only to define historical true-emergence examples for descriptor discovery, never as an operational signal.
At each offset, descriptors use only information available through that date.
Only after per-episode characterization identify common descriptors and explicit regime-specific differences.
Do not force a single generalized recovery signature.
No candidate reentry threshold fitting in this stage.
No CAGR, portfolio drawdown, terminal wealth, or protected-bank fitness.
outputs: candidate descriptor families for later false-rally-vs-durable-recovery testing
qualification: Current-S&P broad-market panel has survivorship qualification; OFR data shifted by two business days.
